notes: Some CLAS components (electromagnetic calorimeter, parts of the time-of-flight wall, forward Cherenkov counters) were reused in CLAS12 according to a search-engine summary of CLAS12 design papers that was not verified here; no reuse is asserted.

placements.note: End year from the 2020 CLAS/CLAS12 review.
placements.quote: Hall B is the site of the CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer (CLAS) detector.

subsystems.quote: The CLAS detector is based on a novel six-coil toroidal magnet which provides a largely azimuthal field distribution.
subsystems.value: Six-coil superconducting toroidal magnet providing a largely azimuthal field

summary.plain: A large, six-sector particle detector built around a toroidal magnet, surrounding the target in Hall B so it could follow almost every particle produced when an electron or photon hit a nucleus.
summary.technical: CEBAF Large Acceptance Spectrometer: six-coil toroidal magnet (largely azimuthal field), drift chambers (0.5% momentum resolution at forward angles), Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters; designed for a luminosity of ~10^34 nucleon cm^-2 s^-1.

technology.quote: The CLAS detector is based on a novel six-coil toroidal magnet which provides a largely azimuthal field distribution.
technology.value: Large-acceptance toroidal-field magnetic spectrometer with drift chambers, Cherenkov counters, time-of-flight scintillators and electromagnetic calorimeters
